summary: Iteration 7 retest of BUG C fix (refund_address REVERTED to REQUIRED on /api/links/pay) + regression of BUG A/B. Backend: 7/7 pytest pass. Frontend: BUG C flows all work — button always visible with disabled:bg-slate-300 styling, label shows '(obligatoire)', empty refund keeps submit disabled (no silent 400), invalid refund shows Sonner toast with backend msg 'Adresse de remboursement invalide.', valid TRC20 → pay-tracker with pay-address/amount/QR. BUG A (dashboard deposit) and BUG B (public link → login → /dashboard) both pass end-to-end. All 3 production bugs confirmed FIXED.

issues: When refund_address is empty, the pay button is truly disabled (HTML disabled attr), so clicking it does NOT fire onClick — the 'Merci de remplir tous les champs' toast requested by the spec cannot appear. If UX intent is 'button clickable to show toast', wrap the button in a div with pointer-events, or make submit unguarded with in-handler validation. Currently the button just stays greyed-out, which is acceptable UX but does not match the spec wording.

action_items: OPTIONAL UX: If you want the 'Merci de remplir tous les champs' toast to actually appear on empty-refund submit attempt, remove the `disabled` HTML attribute and instead perform the emptiness check inside submit() to fire the toast. Currently the disabled button suppresses the click event entirely so the toast branch is unreachable — not a functional bug, but the spec wording implies it should fire.
critical_code_review_comments: PublicLink.js CryptoLinkForm: submit() has a toast branch for empty refund but the button is HTML-disabled, making the branch dead code. Either keep disabled+no toast (current UX) or drop disabled and validate inside submit for toast to actually appear.

rca of the issue: BUG C root cause was that IzichangePay strictly validates refund_address as an on-chain address; the main agent's iter6 attempt to make it optional (mapping empty→'manual-refund') was rejected by the vendor. Iter7 reverts to requiring refund_address (min_length=1 on backend, canSubmit requires refundAddress on UI) while keeping UX improvements: button always visible via disabled:bg-slate-300 styling instead of opacity-0, explicit '(obligatoire)' label with helper text, and Sonner toast on API failure surfacing 'Adresse de remboursement invalide.'.
